title: What is time? (11.14)
hookLine: ask what time it is and someone checks a phone; ask what time is and Augustine admits he doesn't know
tomorrow: two people read one verse two ways. does one have to be wrong?

lines: IF NO ONE ASKS ME, I KNOW.
cards: Ask someone what time it is and they glance at a phone. Ask them what time is, and watch the pause. Augustine hit that same wall, and here's the odd part: he wrote the wall down.
In the Pusey translation: "What then is time? If no one asks me, I know: if I wish to explain it to one that asketh, I know not."
A bishop, in the middle of his own life story, admitting he can't define a word he uses every hour.

teach.b: Book eleven stops telling his life and turns to the first words of Genesis: in the beginning. Which raises a cheeky question. What was God doing before he made heaven and earth?
Augustine says some people answered with a joke, that God was preparing hell for those who pry into deep things. He refuses that answer. He'd rather say plainly, I don't know.
Then he works the puzzle honestly. God made time along with the world, so there was no then before it. But what is time, even now?
The past is gone. The future isn't here yet. And the present, if it stayed, wouldn't be time at all; it slips away the moment you point at it.
His answer: in the mind. There are three times, he says, all of them present. A present of things past: memory.
A present of things present: sight, attention. A present of things future: expectation.
That's the surprise worth repeating tonight. When you dread next month, the month isn't here; your expectation is. When you replay a bad day, the day is over; your memory isn't.
Only attention stands where you actually are.

how: Some Catholics read book eleven of the Confessions slowly as spiritual reading. The Church's tradition of prayer often speaks of the present moment as the place where a person meets God.

o: Augustine's question: known until asked, found in the mind
a sermon on using your hours well before you die
a calendar debate over when the year should begin

p: Augustine: rather say, I don't know

s: Augustine gave a neat, one-line definition of time
he admitted: if no one asks me, I know; if I try to explain, I don't.
Augustine refused the joke that God was preparing hell for people who ask
he'd rather answer plainly that he doesn't know than mock the question.
for Augustine, the future is already out there, waiting
the future isn't yet; it's present only in the mind, as expectation.

games.q: your grandpa says he spends his days "living in the past" and feels guilty about it. what does book eleven offer him?
o: memory is a real way time is present; the past lives on in him now.
the past no longer exists, so remembering it is wasted time.
memory is the only real time, so he should stay there for good.
games.why: Augustine calls memory a present of things past: one of the three ways time lives in the mind, alongside attention and expectation.

practice: Listen for one sound in the room: a fan, traffic, your own breath, and rest on it. Each time your mind slides somewhere else, name it softly, memory or expectation, and come back to the sound that's here.

wordCard.voice: What is time? Augustine's question in book eleven: known until asked, and found in the mind as memory, attention and expectation.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: if no one asks, because some things you know by living them first. Until tomorrow.
